messages:
Alex: Quick follow-up from the RFC — we saw a production case where regional telemetry drops caused the active-active "lease" state to diverge. Not a full split-brain, but tenants started getting writes routed to non-resident regions. :grimacing:
Kira: Ugh. Any logs or repro?
Alex: Yep. I'll paste a short trace. The dataplane accepted a write because the proxy header matched a cached residency flag, but the control-plane lease observer hadn't refreshed due to sampling gaps.
Devon: Can you share the headers + what the control plane thought the lease was?
Alex: Sure — simplified snippet:
```
X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1
X-Tenant-Residency: resident=eu
X-Route-Lease: lease_id=abcd1234;owner=us-west-2
```
Alex: Dataplane checked X-Tenant-Residency and allowed a local short-circuit. Control plane still listed owner=us-west-2 (old).
Sam: So proxy logic is trusting residency header without cross-checking lease freshness? That seems like an interface mismatch.
Kira: Exactly. We intended the proxy to be able to optimistically route by residency but fall back to a lease-check when confidence is low. The confidence calc depends on telemetry windows that are sparse for low-qps tenants.
Eli: Low-qps tenants are the common edge-case. Our current design assumes periodic heartbeats ~30s. If a metric ingest fails for a minute we could misclassify.
Devon: Operationally that's bad because it means writes for PII might leave region. Need a short-term mitigation and a long-term refactor.
Alex: Short-term mitigation idea: add a cheap lease-staleness header check in the proxy. If last_seen_ts - now > 60s, proxy must forward to control-plane-verified owner instead of local.
Kira: +1. We can compute last_seen_ts from our local lease cache. Cheap and incremental.
Sam: Will that add round-trip latency for many requests? For high-qps tenants it won't trigger; for low-qps it will add a single control-plane hop. Acceptable for compliance cases.
Eli: We should make staleness threshold configurable per-tenant (PII vs non-PII). Defaults: 60s for resident-critical, 300s for others.
Devon: Implementational boundary question: should proxy call control-plane lease API directly or call a local runtime agent that synchronizes leases?
Alex: Runtime agent seems cleaner — keeps control-plane API load down and keeps decision logic local. But it's a refactor: currently proxies read from in-memory cache only.
Kira: Long-term refactor proposal: move lease ownership and refresh logic into a small runtime component that shards responsibility per-proxy host. The control plane provides an authoritative stream (gRPC) and the runtime exposes a sync API to local proxies.
Sam: That also buys us a single place for staleness policy and telemetry smoothing. Runtime agent can implement exponential backoff and jitter for leases.
Eli: We need to be careful about trust boundaries. Runtime agent must validate signed lease tokens from the control plane — otherwise a compromised control-plane replica could spoof ownership.
Devon: Good call. Add HMAC-signed lease blobs with epoch and sequence. Runtime verifies signature and sequence monotonicity.
Alex: Action items for short-term: (1) Proxy staleness gate feature flag, default off. (2) Control-plane expose last_seen_ts in lease cache responses. (3) Ops run a canary with 10 tenants in eu-west-1.
Kira: I'll own (1) and (3).
Kira: Drafted config flag: proxy.config.lease_staleness_threshold_seconds (int) and proxy.config.lease_enforcement_mode={optimistic,strict}.
Sam: Who owns the telemetry smoothing change?
Eli: I can take telemetry smoothing; will add a sliding window fallback that synthesizes last_seen from last N heartbeats when metrics are missing.
Devon: Long-term: I'll start a design doc for the runtime agent and signed lease blob format. Will include migration plan and perf targets (max 1ms local lookup, gRPC stream fanout limits).
Alex: One more thing — audit logs. If we route a write out-of-region due to stale info we must emit an audit event with tenant_id, chosen_path, reason=stale_lease. Compliance needs this for forensics.
Sam: +1. Also add alerting rule: "resident-write-out-of-region" when rate > 0 over 15m for PII tenants.
Eli: SRE: we should add a synthetic test that simulates control-plane metric drop and verifies proxy staleness gating routes correctly.
sre-bot: Deploy scheduled: feature flag rollout to canary cluster at 2024-12-02T09:00Z. Steps: enable flag -> monitor audit events -> rollback on >5 incidents/hour.
Alex: OK. I'll write up the short follow-up RFC and link to the runtime-agent doc when Devon starts it.
Kira: Thanks — will post canary cohort list in #eng-runtime. :thumbsup:
Devon: Adding design doc to the repo this afternoon.
Sam: Leaving note for legal about configurable thresholds for regulated tenants.
Alex: Great thread. We'll sync in tomorrow's arch sync for final signoffs.
